metadata.note: The semantic colour layer. Palettes live in themes/bundled/*.theme.json; this file says what each palette entry is FOR, and is the only place a derivation is written. A role's `from` names a theme manifest key (or a `syntax.` / `ansi.` entry); the CSS variable that key writes to is derived (kebab-case), not tabulated. See COLOR.md.

text-disabled.note: disabled non-control text = the default text colour at the `strong` (60%) alpha step — a disabled element inherits its enabled semantic colour, dimmed at the token level, never a dedicated disabled palette value

text-link.note: global.css `a {}` is the only consumer; no component styles a bare link

container-workspace-bg.note: the app surface, and with it the opened-document canvas — a document reads as part of the workspace (Monaco's EDITOR_THEME, the markdown/spec preview, the chat column, the tab strip)

container-content-bg.note: the recessed read-a-diff/read-code canvas, NOT the document canvas (that is workspace): Pierre source diffs, rendered diffs, chat code blocks, and the center-column backdrop behind them

container-elevated-bg.note: every raised surface: dialogs, popovers, menus, toasts, cards, code blocks

control-primary-bg.note: the SOLID primary button fill — its own palette source (`accentSolid`), decoupled from `accent` so a theme can brighten the opaque fill without moving the alpha-derived primary tints (primary-subtle/soft/muted) or the accent used for text/ring/border; every theme maps accentSolid to its accent except regular Light, which uses the brighter dark-theme green

control-primary-bg-hovered.note: the primary button's hover fill — its own manifest key so a theme owns the hover step instead of the button fading with an opacity utility

control-disabled-bg.note: disabled control fill = the default control fill (`input`, i.e. control-bg) at the `strong` (60%) alpha step

control-disabled-text.note: disabled control label/icon = the default control text colour (`text`, i.e. text-default) at the `strong` (60%) alpha step

control-disabled-border.note: disabled control border = the default control border (`border`, i.e. control-border-default) at the `strong` (60%) alpha step

control-primary-disabled-bg.note: disabled primary button fill = the accent hue at the `strong` (60%) alpha step — kept on `accent` (the alpha-tint base), not the brightened solid `accentSolid`, so the disabled fill stays with the primary tint family

control-primary-disabled-text.note: disabled primary button label/icon = the normal primary text (`onAccent`, i.e. control-primary-text) at the `strong` (60%) alpha step

control-destructive-bg.note: the destructive button fill — the feedback-error hue as an opaque control surface

control-soft-primary-bg-hovered.note: the soft-primary button's hover fill: one step past its primary-subtle rest, kept below primary-soft so the accent label stays AA on tinted Light surfaces (themes/schema.test.ts); hover also swaps the border to primary-muted

control-destructive-bg-hovered.note: the destructive button's hover fill — its own manifest key (like accentHover), so hover is a colour step, never an opacity change

control-destructive-text.note: label/icon on the destructive fill; each theme picks it to clear AA on both danger and dangerHover

control-destructive-disabled-bg.note: disabled destructive fill = the enabled fill at the `strong` (60%) alpha step

control-destructive-disabled-text.note: disabled destructive label = the enabled label at the `strong` (60%) alpha step

focus-ring.note: the keyboard focus indicator — the control ring and the active region's line and frame (COLOR.md, Active region); its own role so it can diverge from primary. Full accent is too loud on dark surfaces, so dark appearances take the `firm` (80%) step, which still clears APCA Lc 45 (themes/schema.test.ts)

selection-text.note: nullable in the manifest (high contrast keeps the native foreground)

selection-bg.note: native ::selection in global.css; not a utility

selection-bg-muted.note: the content canvas's ::selection (markdown preview): translucent, so the unselected remainder of a line box reads as a soft edge, not a black hole punched in an opaque wash

editor-selection-text.note: read by Monaco and xterm through getComputedStyle; a utility would be dead weight

editor-selection-highlight-bg.note: Monaco's secondary matches of the active selection

widget-shadow.note: Monaco widget, sticky-scroll, and scrollbar shadows

media-checker-tile.note: the transparency checkerboard tile behind images and vector previews: the text colour at the soft (20%) step — the contrast of the conventional #ccc-on-white checkerboard — over the content canvas, so a dark logo on a transparent PNG stays visible on a dark theme and a light one on a light theme; index.css's `.media-backdrop` is the only consumer

series-1.note: categorical palette (COLOR.md, Categorical series) — blue: the first categorical series (trace: search and discovery tools)

series-2.note: categorical palette (COLOR.md, Categorical series) — orange in every bundled theme but High Contrast Dark (teal): writing tools

series-3.note: categorical palette (COLOR.md, Categorical series) — violet (pale yellow in High Contrast Dark): model calls

series-4.note: categorical palette (COLOR.md, Categorical series) — amber: shell runs; meaning comes from the legend, not from the feedback role it shares a hue with

series-5.note: categorical palette (COLOR.md, Categorical series) — cyan: reading tools

series-6.note: categorical palette (COLOR.md, Categorical series) — magenta: subagents

series-7.note: categorical palette (COLOR.md, Categorical series) — green (blue in High Contrast Dark): planning tools (todo_*, spec_*)

series-8.note: categorical palette (COLOR.md, Categorical series) — neutral grey: the last series, for everything unclassified

ramp-1.note: sequential ramp (COLOR.md, Categorical series): one hue over the alpha scale, low to high; canvas consumers read it, and the action-sequence matrix colours its cells with the first four steps

ramp-2.note: sequential ramp (COLOR.md, Categorical series): one hue over the alpha scale, low to high; canvas consumers read it, and the action-sequence matrix colours its cells with the first four steps

ramp-3.note: sequential ramp (COLOR.md, Categorical series): one hue over the alpha scale, low to high; canvas consumers read it, and the action-sequence matrix colours its cells with the first four steps

ramp-4.note: sequential ramp (COLOR.md, Categorical series): one hue over the alpha scale, low to high; canvas consumers read it, and the action-sequence matrix colours its cells with the first four steps

ramp-5.note: sequential ramp (COLOR.md, Categorical series): one hue over the alpha scale, low to high; canvas consumers read it, and it is published when a DOM chart needs it
